obligations.summary: Deployers that are public-law bodies, private entities providing public services, or deployers of high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III points 5(b) and 5(c) must perform a fundamental rights impact assessment prior to deploying a high-risk AI system referred to in Article 6(2) (except those in Annex III point 2), covering process descriptions, timeframes, affected persons, risks, human oversight measures, and risk mitigation arrangements.
exceptions: High-risk AI systems intended to be used in the area listed in point 2 of Annex III are excluded from this obligation.
In cases referred to in Article 46(1), deployers may be exempt from the obligation to notify the market surveillance authority.

obligations.summary: The fundamental rights impact assessment obligation applies to the first use of the high-risk AI system, and the deployer must update the assessment if any of its elements have changed or are no longer up to date during use.
exceptions: In similar cases, deployers may rely on previously conducted fundamental rights impact assessments or existing impact assessments carried out by the provider instead of conducting a new one.

obligations.summary: Once the fundamental rights impact assessment has been performed, the deployer must notify the market surveillance authority of its results by submitting the filled-out questionnaire template referred to in Article 27(5).
exceptions: Deployers may be exempt from the notification obligation in the case referred to in Article 46(1).

obligations.summary: Where obligations under this Article are already met through a data protection impact assessment conducted pursuant to Article 35 of Regulation (EU) 2016/679 or Article 27 of Directive (EU) 2016/680, the fundamental rights impact assessment must complement that data protection impact assessment.
The AI Office shall develop a questionnaire template, including through an automated tool, to facilitate deployers in complying with their obligations under Article 27 in a simplified manner.
